text: Writing clean code is a skill that makes life easier for everyone who reads your work. The most important goal is readability—your code should be as clear as a well-written sentence. To achieve this, follow strong naming conventions: use descriptive names like `calculateTotalPrice` instead of `ctp` or `x`. Break your program into small, focused functions that each do one thing well. This makes the logic easier to test and debug. When you write clean code, you also improve maintainability, meaning future developers (including yourself) can quickly understand, update, and fix the code without confusion. Ultimately, clean code saves time, reduces errors, and shows respect for your team.
